structured.approach: I read the two contracted inputs: feat.tasks, to find the Data Science lane's tasks and repository, and org.engineering_stack, for languages, the CI command, branch rules and whether Databricks is used. Shell commands are not allowed in DS-01; the G9 hook blocked them. So I relied on the spine's repo-access tool view for availability, the branch's origin and write access. I checked it against the git files in the checkout: HEAD, refs/heads/main, refs/heads/dev, the feature/story reflog and .git/config. I also read ci.py, __init__.py and the function and test names, to record what TSK-03 and TSK-04 will build on. A draft of task.repo_access from an earlier attempt was already in the output folder. I read it before replacing it. It cited the wrong org.engineering_stack commit (3b03f15 instead of b6a392f), so I corrected that. I then wrote task.repo_access in full. I did not use any connector because the inputs and the checkout held every fact I needed.

claims.text: The Data Science lane owns TSK-03 (STORY-03, vendor_risk) and TSK-04 (STORY-04, build_explanation_request risk parameter), both in repository ap_forecast.
ap_forecast is Python 3.9 with unittest and CI command /usr/bin/python3 ci.py; every CI enforces line coverage >= 90%.
No repository uses Databricks or a database, and ap_forecast uses no Databricks or other workspace.
ap_forecast is available locally and the agent identity has write access; git status is clean, so no repository creation is needed.
The working branch feature/story was created from dev at d67e866, and HEAD points to refs/heads/feature/story.
main and dev both point to d67e8662907401467a3f76f9f167e7a60d89ffca, and the feature/story reflog shows it created at that same commit.
Remote origin is configured on GitHub and main and dev track it; feature/story has no upstream configured yet.
Current package version is 0.9.0 and __all__ exports predict_delay_days and build_explanation_request.
ci.py sets COVERAGE_MIN = 90.0, flags print/eval/exec, bare except and lines longer than 140 characters, and imports the third-party coverage package.
Existing tests are test_predict, test_request_uses_config and test_request_with_explicit_config; TSK-03 adds tests/test_risk.py and TSK-04 extends tests/test_forecast.py.
Branch convention is main (released), dev (integration), feature/<story>; commit messages start with the story ID.

open_questions: RAQ-1: Is the third-party coverage package that ci.py imports installed for /usr/bin/python3 on the runner? Interim: assume yes; the first CI run in DS-05/DS-06 confirms it.

RAQ-2: Should STORY-03 and STORY-04 use separate feature/STORY-03 and feature/STORY-04 branches instead of the single provided feature/story? Interim: use feature/story for both, with commit messages that start with the story ID.

It is checked out locally, the agent identity has write access, and the working tree is clean. Work happens on feature/story, which was created from dev at d67e866 and has no commits yet. No repository needs to be created, and no Databricks or database access is needed. I could not run git or CI commands, because shell commands are blocked in this step. Availability and write access therefore come from the spine's repo-access tool view, which I checked against the git files in the checkout. Two non-blocking questions remain. The first is whether the coverage package that ci.py imports is installed for /usr/bin/python3; the first CI run will show this. The second is whether STORY-03 and STORY-04 should get their own branches instead of sharing feature/story.
